transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-02
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 43 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ramirez (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood CSM); Janelle Park (Sundial Head of Platform), Omar Idris (Eng Manager), Leah Brooks (Security Architect)

Auto-summary: quick access and staging readiness check; small talk about Black Friday prep; confirm who will do VPC peering and send credentials; next steps documented.

[00:00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I know a lot to get through so we'll run fast—I'm Maya, AE on the account, Carlos is our SE, Priya is CSM.
[00:00:12] Janelle: Thanks, Maya. Quick note, apologies for starting a minute late, had a sync with ops. We're in a bit of a rush since we've got Black Fri scheduling in a couple weeks.
[00:00:25] Priya: Totally—we just want to make sure the activation path is clear and that staging can exercise the key paths.
[00:00:33] Omar: Also want to make sure we don't accidentally hit prod-level quotas. We'll be testing on a reserved sandbox.
[00:00:40] Carlos: Great, we'll walk through the runbook items. First item: access. We issued temporary API keys and a short lived key for staging—Maya will send those out.
[00:00:56] Janelle: Perfect, can you remind me the token format and if there are IP allow lists?
[00:01:04] Maya: The keys arrive as a single header bearer token, sample curl in the runbook; for the staging flow we also support IP allow list and VPC peering. For now we'll do IP allow list then move to peering when network is ready.
[00:01:20] Leah: On the security side, we need to confirm key rotation and whether keys are logged. Are these keys stored in your KMS or ours?
[00:01:30] Carlos: For Redwood Hosted, keys are tenant-scoped and we integrate with customer KMS for Private deployments. For Hosted/early staging keys we keep them ephemeral and they are not persisted in plaintext—we'll share the key rotation policy doc.
[00:01:44] Omar: So if we go Redwood Private in future, we can plug into our HSM?
[00:01:48] Carlos: Yep, Private supports external KMS/HSM and you can bring your own key material. There's also Dedicated option if you need reserved GPUs.
[00:01:56] Janelle: Understood. Next, networking—Omar, you had questions about peering?
[00:02:03] Omar: Yeah, what exact CIDRs do you need and do you need a static egress IP? We have strict firewall egress rules.
[00:02:11] Maya: We can do two options: IP allowlist or VPC peering. For peering we need a /24 range for the peer endpoints and a list of NATs if egress is necessary. We'll include a CIDR template in the runbook.
[00:02:27] Omar: Okay, I'll get that from infra and share.
[00:02:31] Priya: Note to put that in action items—Omar to share CIDR and firewall contact.
[00:02:37] [00:05:10] Carlos: Moving to smoke tests—basic paths you should run: 1) token auth + simple generation (100 token typical load), 2) batch embedding job small runs, 3) chat context replay using KV cache verify. We'll provide a small load script.
[00:05:28] Leah: KV cash? Did you mean KV cache?
[00:05:31] Carlos: Sorry yes, KV cache—transcription wonky there.
[00:05:35] Janelle: For the tests, we'll try to emulate peak user concurrency to see latency; what's your expected latency for a 256-token generation on the hosted profile?
[00:05:46] Carlos: On our verified profile, 256 tokens on a medium LLM comes in around 200–300 ms per token at steady state but depends on batching. For single-request latency we see 400–800 ms round trip usually; we'll include perf knobs in the runbook.
[00:06:05] Omar: If we need consistent p95 under 1s we probably want Dedicated or pinned instances right?
[00:06:12] Maya: Yes, dedicated pools and pinned models reduce variance; we can propose a small Dedicated pool for your peak windows, but for now staging on Hosted with peering should suffice to validate flows.
[00:06:24] [00:08:02] Leah: Compliance—SOC2 evidence you mentioned, what bundle do you provide?
[00:08:08] Priya: We typically share an evidence bundle including SOC2 report, encryption at rest docs, pen test summary, and data retention policy. We'll send the package to Leah's email.
[00:08:20] Leah: Also we need audit log retention details, especially token-level tracing.
[00:08:26] Carlos: Audit logs include request metadata, timestamps, model version, and per-request token counts; retention varies by tier but we can configure a short-term retention for staging and longer for production.
[00:08:38] Janelle: Can logs be exported to our SIEM?
[00:08:41] Carlos: Yep, we support log forwarders (S3, syslog, or direct API hooks).
[00:08:47] [00:12:15] Maya: Small note—billing and usage expectations for staging. We'll provide a test credit estimate. For early smoke tests expect under $150 of usage unless you run heavy batch embedding.
[00:12:27] Omar: Good to know. We'll gate heavy batch jobs behind an internal flag.
[00:12:32] Janelle: About role-based access—how do you do RBAC and team separation in the console?
[00:12:39] Priya: Console supports org-level admins, project-level roles with read/write deploy, and token-scoped roles. We can demo role bindings if helpful.
[00:12:49] Leah: Need SAML SSO integration details as well.
[00:12:52] Maya: We have a SAML guide; for staging we'll do email-based invites then configure SSO for production.
[00:12:59] [00:16:00] Omar: One more item—rollouts. We plan to canary to 5% of traffic. Does Redwood support traffic splitting?
[00:16:07] Carlos: Yes, we support canary rollouts and automatic fallback. You can route by percentage or by request attributes; our console shows per-route metrics so you can watch quality/regressions.
[00:16:18] Janelle: Are we able to pin a model version? We need repeatable outputs.
[00:16:22] Carlos: Absolutely, version pinning is available and part of the rollout policy.
[00:16:27] [00:20:10] Priya: Quick check—who will be the primary contact for day-of troubleshooting during the staging run?
[00:20:16] Omar: That would be me for infra and Janelle for product.
[00:20:19] Priya: OK we'll send an on-call list in the runbook.
[00:20:23] [00:24:01] Janelle: Can we get a sample observability dashboard or the metrics you expose?
[00:24:06] Carlos: Yes, we have per-token cost breakdowns, latency histograms, per-model QPS, and error rates. We'll share a sample dashboard screenshot and the JSON export so you can import.
[00:24:18] Leah: Any private data path considerations? We need assurance PII isn't logged during tests.
[00:24:25] Carlos: You can enable redaction and a privacy mode that prevents storing request/response bodies in logs; we also support request-side obfuscation. For PII-heavy workloads we'd recommend Private deployment.
[00:24:40] [00:28:30] Maya: Ok wrapping to next steps—I'll send staging runbook with curl samples, cidr template, and a follow-up calendar invite for the smoke test window. Carlos will send the load script.
[00:28:40] Janelle: Sounds good. One ask—can we have a short 30-minute dry run before the big smoke test?
[00:28:47] Maya: Yes, absolutely. We'll schedule a 30-min dry run the week before your smoke test.
[00:28:54] Omar: I'll coordinate dates and reply to the invite.
[00:28:58] [00:32:10] Priya: I'll upload the SOC2 package to the shared folder and tag Leah.
[00:32:15] Leah: Thanks, I'll review and send back any gaps.
[00:32:19] [00:36:05] Carlos: Misc note—if you want to experiment with quantized models to reduce cost we can suggest a quantization profile for embeddings.
[00:36:13] Janelle: That's interesting—maybe after staging once we see perf.
[00:36:18] Maya: Great. Any final questions?
[00:36:22] Omar: None from infra.
[00:36:24] Leah: All good for now.
[00:36:27] Janelle: No, thanks everyone.
[00:36:31] Maya: Thanks, we'll send the runbook and keys. Recap: Maya sends runbook+keys, Omar shares CIDR, Carlos sends load script, Leah reviews SOC2 artifacts. We'll plan a dry run before full smoke.
[00:36:51] Maya: Thanks all, talk soon.
[00:36:55] [End of transcript]
